set.body:
Introduce the exact discrete-view algebra and minimum codomain field algebra without duplicating Ravel.

Exact view requirements
- Represent only maps that can be proven against geometry and, for the zero-copy surface, represented by Ravel strides: identity, crop, signed permutation/flip, per-axis stride, and supported axis drops.
- Broader exact maps must state and test materialization explicitly.
- Geometry is derived by composing the source embedding/affine with the discrete map.
- Existing crop/select methods delegate to this common mechanism or are compatibility facades over it.

Field operations
- mapValues with explicit output semantics.
- same-owner zipWith and alignment-consuming zipWithAligned.
- replaceDataChecked.
- coordinate-aware axis permutation/selection.
- reduction scaffolding for operations whose result remains a rectangular Sampled space; irregular grouping stays with locus4s.

Acceptance criteria
- Ravel continues to own every storage/layout operation and numerical kernel.
- image4s proves that the Ravel view and target sampling geometry agree.
- Zero-copy methods never materialize.
- Materializing methods are named and allocation-tested.
- No filter catalogue, second IR, or second runtime enters core.

Tests
- map identity and composition laws.
- exact-view identity and composition.
- crop composition, flip involution, permutation inverse, and stride-coordinate properties.
- source/target physical-coordinate equality at every sampled target index for generated small grids.
- canonical-layout idempotence and materialized-copy extensional equality.
- aligned zipWith pointwise oracle and failure cases.
- Allocation/storage-sharing tests for every zero-copy view on JVM plus logical parity on Scala.js.
- Negative tests reject non-representable maps from the zero-copy API.
set.title: Complete the exact-view and minimal sampled-field algebra
